title: 射雕英雄传 · 华山论剑
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create ONE exquisite standalone vintage watercolor wuxia landscape poster, portrait 4:5, an illustrated collector's edition inspired by Jin Yong's novels. This belongs to a coherent eight-print collection.
Style: warm ivory aged paper, subtle paper fibers, fine expressive pen lines beneath transparent watercolor, layered mineral greens and dusty blue, warm ochre with restrained vermilion accents. Sophisticated atmospheric perspective, intricate but credible period architecture and tiny expressive figures. A single continuous grand landscape with foreground, middle distance and distant mountains or horizon; no panels. Let the environment occupy about 85 percent of the artwork. Human scale should convey epic vastness. Hand-painted illustration, rich detail yet breathing room. Soft faded paper margins, delicate thin corner ornament.
Typography: reserve a small clear header area, small Chinese novel name above a larger elegant dark-brown Chinese calligraphic scene title, and a tiny widely spaced English subtitle. Render the specified Chinese text accurately. No other labels or prose.
All people wear plausible Song-period Chinese or early Mongol/Central Asian clothing as appropriate. Fictional literary visualization, not a historical documentary or adaptation screenshot. No modern objects, no firearms, no luminous energy beams, no flying dragons, no photorealism, no 3D plinth, no comic panels, no watermark.

Novel header (exact): "射雕英雄传". Main title (exact): "华山论剑". English subtitle (exact): "SUMMIT OF LEGENDS".
Scene: The legendary FIRST Mount Hua gathering, a conceptual tableau of the five great martial masters, NOT a tournament arena: towering sheer granite peaks, narrow snow-dusted stone ledges, a sea of cloud, twisted pines, immense distant ridges. Exactly FIVE small separated masters on a broad connected summit platform: a composed Daoist in dark simple robes (Wang Chongyang), a lean green-robed flute bearer (Huang Yaoshi), a white-robed western martial master with a staff (Ouyang Feng), a dignified southern ruler in restrained regal robes (Duan Zhixing, BEFORE becoming a monk), and a patched-robed beggar holding a bamboo staff (Hong Qigong). They regard one another, no need for synchronized attacks. No Guo Jing here. Sunrise above clouds, serene, lofty, monumental.
